answer: Each agent presents a hardware-rooted attestation proving its enclave runs code matching an approved MRENCLAVE, and binds its identity key to a hardware-protected secret. This raises the cost of Sybil identities: copying a VM cannot reproduce that secret or forge the quote, so scaling identities requires access to genuine attested silicon. MRENCLAVE alone is not unique per device; enforcement must also verify key binding and attestation policy. The voyage across basalt is no reason to wander from that distinction.
